terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Blue screen of death (BSOD)
terms.definition: Causes can stem from bad hardware, bad drivers, or application issues that prevent the OS from continuing.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Boot issues
terms.definition: Check for missing OS/bootloader issues or dual-boot conflicts. Remove any attached non-bootable media.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: “No OS found”
terms.definition: Caused by bootloader corruption, dual-boot overwrites, or missing boot files.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Degraded performance
terms.definition: Use Task Manager (Processes tab and 60-second Performance tab view) to identify resource-hogging apps.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Low memory warnings
terms.definition: Sort Task Manager by the Memory column to locate memory-draining programs. Save files and close or restart open programs.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Frequent shutdowns
terms.definition: Run full hardware diagnostics (motherboard, CPU, RAM) via UEFI/BIOS, motherboard tools, or Windows Memory Diagnostics.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: System instability
terms.definition: Occurs randomly without warning.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Time drift
terms.definition: Caused by hardware inaccurate timekeeping.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Services not starting
terms.definition: Verify device status in Device Manager — update, roll back, or replace drivers.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Applications crashing
terms.definition: Inspect log entries in Event Viewer or use Reliability Monitor to identify failure causes and performance trends over time.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: USB controller resource warnings
terms.definition: This occurs when connecting devices that exceed the USB controller’s available endpoints.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS Problems
terms.name: Slow profile load
terms.definition: Typically caused by network latency or WAN congestion when syncing roaming user profiles to a remote domain controller.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to launch
terms.definition: Restart the mobile device to clear memory and stored caches Check for and install application updates to fix potential software bugs Delete and reinstall the application from the app store

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to close / crashes
terms.definition: Force close the application — slide it off the app list on iOS, or select Force Stop in Android Settings — and reopen it.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to update
terms.definition: Manually trigger the update or choose Update All in the app store Verify a valid, current payment method is on file Check network/internet connectivity Verify sufficient available storage space Restart the device to clear pending updates Check for Mobile Device Management (MDM) corporate policy restrictions or app store outages MDM App store Storage

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Application fails to install
terms.definition: Check for sufficient free storage space Ensure a valid payment method is configured in the app store account Verify network connectivity or move to an unfiltered network Confirm MDM policies permit application installation

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Slow to respond
terms.definition: Perform a device restart to free up resources and clear cache Update the application or operating system to resolve underlying bugs

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: OS fails to update
terms.definition: Free up storage space — OS patches require significant capacity Connect to a high-speed network with adequate bandwidth Change networks if content filtering blocks update servers Restart the device and attempt the update again

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Battery life issues
terms.definition: Enable Airplane Mode in low or no coverage areas to stop the radio from constantly searching for a signal Turn off unused features like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or GPS Check battery health and usage history under Settings > Battery Replace old or degraded batteries

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Random reboots
terms.definition: Update the OS and all installed applications Review crash logs or contact support to check for underlying hardware failures Inspect battery health

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Connectivity issues — Wi-Fi
terms.definition: Ensure Wi-Fi is toggled on Verify security keys and settings match the access point Move closer to the access point or connect to a different network Restart the mobile device

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Connectivity issues — Bluetooth
terms.definition: Confirm Bluetooth is enabled Toggle Bluetooth off and on, or restart the device to re-establish pairings Ensure Bluetooth (and Wi-Fi) are enabled when using proximity tools like AirDrop, and move devices closer together

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Connectivity issues — Near-field communication (NFC)
terms.definition: Toggle NFC off and on Restart the device Ensure linked credit cards and payment details are up to date

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Issues
terms.name: Screen does not autorotate
terms.definition: Check if the screen orientation lock is enabled Close and reopen the stuck application Restart the mobile device Contact device support if the internal G-sensor/accelerometer hardware has failed

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Application source / unofficial application stores
terms.definition: Sideloading apps from third-party sites or APK files poses severe security risks because uncurated sources may contain malware that can access device data.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Developer mode
terms.definition: Enables advanced OS access, USB debugging, memory statistics, and detailed logging capabilities.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Root access / jailbreak
terms.definition: Modifies core firmware to override the factory operating system, granting complete control over the device and enabling sideloading.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Unauthorized / malicious application
terms.definition: Unapproved apps or infected development environments (e.g., XcodeGhost) can inject malicious code, harvest data, or secretly sign users up for paid services without consent.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Application spoofing
terms.definition: Malicious apps masquerade as legitimate tools (e.g., photo editors or QR scanners) while performing hidden malicious actions in the background.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: High network traffic
terms.definition: Unexpected spikes in data transmission can indicate a malware infection, such as command-and-control communications or encrypted traffic proxying.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Degraded response time
terms.definition: Unresponsive screens, sluggish app performance, or choppy animations can be caused by resource-heavy malware or buggy software.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Data-usage limit notification
terms.definition: Reaching a cellular data threshold — using native Android limits/warnings or third-party monitoring apps — can serve as an early warning sign that background malware is exfiltrating data.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Limited internet connectivity
terms.definition: Malware or misconfigurations can degrade network performance.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: No internet connectivity
terms.definition: Malware may intentionally block internet connections to prevent anti-malware definition updates or security software downloads.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: High number of ads
terms.definition: Persistent or excessive ad pop-ups are often driven by adware or fake ad-blocking malware (e.g., Fake Ads Block) designed to generate ad revenue for attackers.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Fake security warnings
terms.definition: Malicious browser pop-ups imitate official system alerts to trick users into downloading “security updates” that actually install malware.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Unexpected application behavior
terms.definition: Sudden crashes, unresponsiveness, broken features, or excessive battery drain are typically app-specific bugs.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Mobile OS and Application Security Issues
terms.name: Leaked personal files / data
terms.definition: Caused by local malware breaches or compromised cloud storage accounts.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Unable to access the network
terms.definition: Malware can intentionally block network access to prevent downloading anti-malware tools or installing operating system security patches that close known vulnerabilities.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Desktop alerts
terms.definition: Rogue browser pop-ups or pushed web messages often impersonate official system notifications to trick users into extending fake subscriptions or downloading malicious software.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: False alerts regarding antivirus protection
terms.definition: Scareware mimics legitimate security tools, claiming your system is disabled or infected with specific threats (e.g., Trojan spyware). They direct users to call fake tech support numbers or pay money.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Altered system or personal files
terms.definition: Files or system binaries are unexpectedly renamed, moved, or missing.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Unwanted notifications within the OS
terms.definition: Operating systems allow apps to push unwanted pop-ups.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: OS update failures
terms.definition: Malware, network misconfigurations, firewall filtering rules, or network bandwidth caps can block system updates.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Random / frequent pop-ups
terms.definition: Fake application prompts appear despite modern browser pop-up blockers being enabled by default.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Certificate warnings
terms.definition: Browsers display “connection is not private” or untrusted site errors. Click the lock icon next to the HTTPS URL to inspect certificate details.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Redirection
terms.definition: Entering a search query or URL redirects the user to unintended, illegitimate websites designed to display ads or distribute further malware.

terms.sectionTitle: Troubleshoot Windows OS Security Issues
terms.name: Degraded browser performance
terms.definition: Sluggish loading and high system resource usage can be caused by excessive open tabs, bloated browser caches, or malicious JavaScript (e.g., background crypto miners using 100% CPU).
